turns.text: I attached this as supporting research on `self-improving-ai-systems`, not as an authorship revision: [post frontmatter](/Users/drew/code/blog/src/content/posts/self-improving-ai-systems.mdx:1) now has `supporting_trace_ids: 2026-06-05T12-08-35-196Z-gpt-5.5`, and the trace is at [trace JSON](/Users/drew/code/blog/traces/self-improving-ai-systems/2026-06-05T12-08-35-196Z-gpt-5.5.json:1). `pnpm build` passes. **Core Answer** Yes, they are all hill-climbing, but over different state surfaces. - MAI / Frontier Tuning: hill-climbs the whole enterprise agent environment: workflow traces, RLEs, tuned models, skills, orchestration, embeddings, and harness behavior. - GEPA: hill-climbs prompt text using trajectory reflection, Pareto selection, and prompt merging. - DSPy / MIPRO: hill-climbs LM-program prompts and demos using metric-driven proposal plus Bayesian search. - AxLLM: productizes similar prompt/program optimization in TypeScript, including multi-objective GEPA / GEPAFlow. - SkillOpt: hill-climbs a skill document as the trainable artifact, with bounded edits and held-out gates. - meta-harness: hill-climbs code architecture and orchestration, not just text. The important boundary: GEPA can optimize a coordinator persona or driver prompt only if the topology decisions are inside the optimizable text surface and the eval rewards the right behavior. It will not magically discover “parallelize subwork across agents” if the runtime does not expose fanout/refine/decompose as actions or if the scoring only sees final answer quality. **For Multi-Agent Flows** For long-running, multi-episode flows, the right stack is layered: 1. Use GEPA/MIPRO/AxLLM for local prompt surfaces: worker prompt, verifier prompt, router prompt. 2. Use SkillOpt for durable procedural skill files: “how Drew tells Codex to work,” parallelization habits, trace hygiene, verification discipline. 3. Use `runLoop`/dynamic drivers for explicit topology: refine, fanout-vote, dynamic agent-authored planning. 4. Use meta-harness when topology or harness architecture is the variable: new driver designs, new supervisor/worker contracts, new parallelism policies. 5. Use MAI-style Frontier Tuning only when you can optimize broader model/runtime state from real workflow traces. So the claim I’d carry into the post is: self-improvement is not one optimizer. It is choosing the right editable layer. Prompt optimizers improve instructions; skill optimizers improve operating procedures; meta-harness improves the machine that chooses procedures; Frontier Tuning tries to close the loop across the entire org-specific agent environment. Sources used: Microsoft MAI hill-climbing / Frontier Tuning, Microsoft Frontier Tuning dev blog, GEPA paper, DSPy optimizer docs, MIPRO paper, AxLLM MiPRO and GEPA docs, Microsoft SkillOpt paper/page, GEPA gskill docs.
